Why Marketers Shouldn’t Treat Every Frown From Legal Like a Stop Sign

Plus, how New Belgium Brewing’s Shaun Belongie navigated his way from marketing chief to the top job

By

, WSJ Leadership Institute

Good morning. A “no” from a company’s general counsel shouldn’t be the end of the conversation for marketing teams.

That’s because detecting risk and assessing it aren’t necessarily the same thing, attendees heard Tuesday at the opening day of the Leadership Institute’s WSJ CMO Council Summit.

“Too often people say no because there’s a risk—and that risk could be a speeding ticket instead of a felony,” said Jonathan Adashek, senior vice president and chief global affairs officer at IBM. “Those are very different things.”

“… This is something I deal with inside my team all the time: ‘Lawyer said no.’ No, the lawyer didn’t say no,” Adashek said. “The lawyer told you there’s a risk. You are saying no.”
